boundary_decision.rationale: Personal, project, organizational and public budgets share a governed resource-plan core, while appropriation, fiscal transparency, accounting and jurisdictional obligations remain explicit optional profiles and execution systems retain mastership of actual events.

decisions.rationale: An authorized budget records plan or authority while a forecast records a current expectation; neither may silently replace the other.
Proposal, ceiling, approved, allocated, available, committed, obligated, actual, paid and cash amounts retain separate bases, authorities and evidence.
A public appropriation or another legal authorization is not universal and does not itself prove a commitment, obligation, expense or payment.
Cash, accrual, commitment and GFSM statistical views may legitimately differ and must be mapped with versions and loss rather than collapsed.
Ledger entries, contracts, procurements, invoices, payments and revenue collections keep authoritative external identity and lifecycle.
The budget owns scoped resource bindings but not organization, programme, project, activity, beneficiary or performance-evidence master lifecycles.
All profiles need owner, scope, period, classifications, estimates, changes and comparisons, while public-sector authority and transparency rules remain conditional.

decisions.disposition: accepted as public-sector and policy profile
decisions.rationale: GIFT, OECD and EU references support accountable publication and participation without imposing public-law obligations on every private budget.
Transfers, supplementary budgets, carryovers, lapses, freezes and releases require authority, reason and effective time and never overwrite the authorized predecessor.
Spending may be compared with outputs and outcomes, but expenditure alone cannot establish effectiveness, value for money or causal impact.
Budget is an informational planning object; its direct properties are identity, owner, purpose, scope, period, basis, currency, status, version and amounts rather than physical attributes.

The structure covers identity, direct informational properties, formulation, authority, controlled actions, execution bindings, evidence, validation, provenance, access, reporting and lifecycle, but specialist profiles still require refinement.
